content.text:
Root cause: `Sources/BarTimeTrackerCore/TimeCalculations.swift:74` — `firstOn` = *first* `on`/`screensaverOff` event of day, no filtering.

Today log has power-nap dark wakes:
```
2026-09-14,01:04:52,on,computer,-
2026-09-14,01:04:52,off,computer,-   <- same second
...repeats 01:24, 01:40, 01:55, 02:45, 03:34, 04:47, 05:35, 06:36
2026-09-14,07:20:40,on   (off 07:21:10)
2026-09-14,08:05:57,on   <- real start
```
Machine woke for maintenance at 01:04, slept right back. Span start anchors there, so day reads 01:04.

Fix options:
1. Drop `on` events whose paired `off` comes within ~1-2 min (dark wake, no real session).
2. Anchor first span to last `on`/`screensaverOff` before first project entry instead of first of day.

Option 2 more robust — say word, me implement.
We're going withn 2. Never drop recordings, that destroys data. Only the human operator can do that.

content.text:
Work periods implemented (uncommitted, not rebuilt).

`TimeCalculations.buildWorkPeriods(from:projectEntries:absenceThreshold:now:)` — collapses every project to Work/Break, builds spans on that, drops Break spans, then cuts any period where the computer was off ≥5 min. `addDayItems` now renders those rows; submenu still shows per-project totals inside the period.

Today's menu becomes roughly: `08:05 – 12:37` (Qamcorder + AI Dev), break, `13:36 – 14:15` (Fineasity + Qamcorder), break, `14:31 – …` — instead of 14 rows.

Two side fixes needed to get there:
- `test_may29_spans` was flaky (passed ~2 of 3 runs) — ties in `projectDurations` sorted in dictionary order. Equal durations now break by who started first in the span; `dailyProjectTotals` breaks by name. 37/37 stable across 3 runs.
- New `test_jun1_workPeriods` locks the merged output.

Known leftover, pre-existing: the tail between the last work entry and the off is attributed to the *next* entry, so Jun 1's afternoon period shows `Break 16m` inside it. Say word if you want that tail to stay with the project instead.

Run `./build.sh && ./restart.sh` when you want to see it.
